gaps.property: Property 7 / module-spec rule 7 (dependencies and their real APIs) — named API does not exist at the path given
gaps.problem: §7 addresses every dependency api as `ctx.modules.<dep>.api.<fn>()` — 'ctx.modules.terrain.api: data(), stats()…', 'ctx.modules.roads.api: rebuild()…', 'ctx.modules.buildings.api: requestSpawn(lot)…', 'ctx.modules.simulation.api', 'ctx.modules.environment.api', and 'ctx.modules.props?.api?.stats?.()'. That path is undefined. registry.js:36 passes `modules: this.apis` and registry.js:14 stores the api object directly, so the real path is `ctx.modules.roads.rebuild()`. Every shipped module uses the short form (buildings/showcase.js:70, zoning/index.js:143, props/index.js:256). The spec contradicts itself: §8 correctly writes `ctx.modules.roads?.rebuild?.()` and `ctx.modules.buildings?.spawnFreeLots?.()`, and §2 correctly writes `ctx.modules.services`. Combined with BUILDER.md's mandated optional chaining, a builder who follows §7 writes `ctx.modules.roads?.api?.rebuild?.()`, which silently no-ops — no road rebuild means no frontage, no isRoad mask, no components, and coverage/validate/showcase all fail for a reason that looks like a logic bug. This is the one section whose entire purpose is 'the exact functions, so nothing is invented'.
gaps.fix: Rewrite every §7 heading to the real path: 'ctx.modules.terrain: data() · stats() · material() · setGrassTufts(enabled) · setReflection(enabled) · debug.*', and likewise for roads, zoning, buildings, simulation, environment and props. Add one line: '`ctx.modules` is the api object per module (registry.js:36 `modules: this.apis`) — there is no `.api` sub-object; `ctx.modules.roads.api` is undefined.' Fix the same error in BUILDER.md's 'Fail soft' bullet so it does not drift back.

gaps.property: Property 4 (anchored) and 2 (falsifiable) — five acceptance items are graded in shots whose framing the spec forbids the module to control and never pins by coordinate
gaps.problem: Items 5, 7, 10, 19 and 20 are graded at `closeup_12`, `street_12`, `street_22`, `aerial_12`/`aerial_17p5` and `skyline_12` — all standard-matrix cameras. Those are core presets with fixed targets: closeup = distance 110, target [20,6,20]; street = distance 60, target [40,0,40]; aerial = 520, [0,0,0]; skyline = 900, [0,40,0] (camera.js:22-29). §8 says the module declares 'exactly these six names' (utilities, plant_close, civic, park, coverage, night_civic), which forbids overriding them — even though main.js:95-98 registers `showcase.cameras` before setup and ARCHITECTURE §4 explicitly allows 'optional overrides of core presets'. §8 then describes the layout only as 'utilities on the west, civic street on the east, a green core', with no coordinates. So whether item 7's recessed windows and canopied entrance are even in frame at closeup_12 is left to luck, and items 5 and 10 both grade `street_*` — one wants the large park's lawn, paths and benches in that frame, the other wants civic window grids and a floodlit yard, from the same fixed target (40,0,40). Two competent builders produce two different districts and one of them fails item 7 on staging, not on quality.
gaps.fix: Either (a) name the staging coordinates: 'the civic street runs north-south through x ≈ 20–60, so the core `closeup` target [20,6,20] lands on the clinic facade; the large park's main path passes within 40 m of [40,0,40]; the utilities yard is centred near x ≈ -400 and is framed by `utilities`', or (b) drop 'exactly these six names', let `showcase.cameras` override aerial/street/skyline/closeup with framings that put the graded content in shot, and state what each override must contain. Then re-point item 10's night grading at `night_civic_22` plus a declared override rather than the core `street`.

gaps.problem: §8 tells the builder to call `ctx.modules.buildings?.spawnFreeLots?.(≤ 120)` and then requires '≥ 120 buildings on the surrounding blocks so demand is non-zero and served.* is meaningful'. Only exactly 120 satisfies both, and spawnFreeLots returns fewer when free lots run out, so the requirement is unsatisfiable in the normal case — while item 15's scene budget (≤ 300 draw calls with roads 80 + terrain 20 + env 15 + zoning 10 + services 60 already committed) pushes the other way. Separately, '≥ 22 items total (2 wind turbines beyond the first, 2 extra parks)' adds up to 21, and the next bullet demands 'a wind row of ≥ 4 turbines' (3 beyond the first), contradicting the parenthetical.
gaps.fix: Replace with a single reconciled number: 'stage 140–180 free lots and call spawnFreeLots(160); ≥ 120 buildings must exist in stats() and the scene must still read ≤ 300 draw calls — if it does not, cut lots, not services.' Fix the item count to '≥ 22 items: the 17 kinds plus 3 extra wind turbines (≥ 4 in the row) and 2 extra parks'.

gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) — item 5's counts have no observation method
gaps.problem: Item 5 demands '≥ 24 trees of ≥ 3 species with ≥ 4 crown-colour variants and no two adjacent instances sharing rotation and scale; ≥ 8 benches, ≥ 4 bins, ≥ 6 path lamps; a hedge or low wall on ≥ 60 % of the perimeter', 'verifiable by eye and by `stats().kinds`'. But §2 defines `stats().kinds` as `{<kind>:n}` over the 17 service kinds — it cannot report a single tree, bench, bin or lamp. Every one of these numbers therefore collapses to 'by eye', which is exactly the argued round the checklist exists to prevent (a critic counting benches in a 90 m street shot will miss occluded ones and the builder will dispute it). Item 12's '≥ 20 % of park-vegetation instance transforms differ — probe a hash of the first 64 tree matrices' has the same problem: none of the 18 declared api functions exposes tree matrices, and the spec never says to reach them through `window.__sim.registry.modules.get('services').group`.
gaps.fix: Add to the required `stats()` shape: `decor:{trees, treeSpecies, crownVariants, benches, bins, pathLamps, hedgeSegments, hedgePerimeterFrac, parkedVehicles}` and a 19th api function `debug.instanceHash(kind, n)` returning a stable hash of the first n instance matrices. Then restate items 5 and 12 against those fields.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — `load` and kind-key coverage are undefined for the two-category producer
gaps.problem: §2 defines `load` for 'a producer of category c' but `load` is a scalar on the item and `incinerator` has `capacity {garbage:700, power:120}` — the spec never says which c it reports. Item 13(e) inherits the hole ('each item's load ≤ its effectiveCapacity for that category'). The same gap appears in the coverage key table: 'any of the 17 kinds → the formula above, restricted to facilities of that kind alone' does not say which category's supply/demand ratio a utility kind key uses, so `coverage('incinerator', x, z)` and `coverage('power_wind', x, z)` are undefined — and because §5 exempts those six from the grid and item 3(a) only checks 'finite in [0,1]', any answer passes and the divergence stays invisible until infoviews or tools consume it.
gaps.fix: Add: 'a multi-category producer reports `load` for its largest capacity category (incinerator → garbage), and `item.loadBy` is an optional per-category object'; and to the key table: 'a utility kind key returns the component ratio for that kind''s primary category with the numerator restricted to producers of that kind — incinerator uses garbage — and is documented as a diagnostic, not a game input.'

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — the texture-memory ceiling is unmeasurable and inconsistent with the count it sits next to
gaps.problem: §5 says 'GPU texture memory: ≤ 64 MB is the real ceiling; ≤ 16 textures created by this module, none above 2048²', measured by 'probe stats().textures'. `stats().textures` is defined in §2 as a count of THREE.Texture objects — it cannot report megabytes, so the 64 MB number has no named observation method (property 2). Worse, the two are inconsistent: 16 textures at 2048² RGBA is about 268 MB, over four times the stated ceiling, so a builder can satisfy the checkable constraint and blow the stated one by 4× with no item failing.
gaps.fix: Either drop the 64 MB line, or make it derivable: 'at most 16 textures; at most two at 2048² and the rest ≤ 1024², which bounds this module at ≤ 64 MB — `stats().textureBytes` must report the sum of width×height×bytesPerPixel×1.33 and be ≤ 64 × 1024².'

gaps.property: Module-spec rule 8 / cross-module ownership — the props collision in the integrated build is reasoned up to and then left open
gaps.problem: §7 correctly establishes that props is absent at ?showcase=services and hands park vegetation to this module. But at `--showcase all` and in democity both modules are loaded, and props/place.js only avoids zoned lots (its 'lot occupancy' guard at place.js:60) — service pads are not zoned lots, so props' rebuild() will grow forest through the coal plant pad, the school yard and the fire apron. BUILDER.md's definition of done includes a clean `--showcase all` shot, so this lands on this builder with no stated remedy and no acceptance item covering it.
gaps.fix: Add one line to §7 and one acceptance item: 'services must publish its pad footprints where props can see them — either by zoning-erasing the pad cells in place() or by a `docs/core-requests/services.md` asking props for a keep-out list; the `--showcase all` aerial must show no tree standing inside a service footprint.'

gaps.problem: §4's preamble enumerates BUILDER.md's engineering rules ('determinism through ctx.rng (no Math.random, no Date.now() in logic), instancing, no per-frame allocation, lane discipline, colour space, zero console errors…, status ready everywhere, draw calls within budget'), and §5's closing paragraph repeats 'a per-object Mesh for repeated content is an automatic budget fail' and 'nothing in this module allocates per frame' from the same file. strengths: Almost every factual claim about the repo checks out against the code. world.services at src/core/world.js:94-103 (exact lines), the 17 kinds byte-identical to world.js and ui/hud.js, all 17 cost/label/cat/unlock values in §4.2 match SERVICE_KINDS exactly, economy.js:355 is the growth gate, economy.js:227 with TICKS_PER_HOUR=100/GRID_TICK=50 makes the '110 ticks' figure in item 13(d) arithmetically right, and the '12 288 coverage() calls per game hour' is 64² × 3 park kinds from grids.js:119 — verified.

The 13 coverage keys the spec says simulation queries are exactly the 13 queried in economy.js:_refreshEnvironment (school/high_school/university/clinic/hospital/police/fire/park_small/park_large/plaza/power/water/garbage), which makes §5's '14 grids = those 13 + sewage' derivation correct rather than a guess.

One coverage formula, defined once in §2, with an explicit 'nothing in §4 redefines it' and a single named degrade path. This is the single best structural decision in the file — it removes the usual round-1 argument about what coverage means.

Known failure modes are real and correctly cited: roads_r1 #2/#5/#6, environment_r1 #3/#7, environment_r2 #2, effects_r1 #2/#4/#5/#7, terrain_r1 #4/#8, simulation_r1 #7/#8 all match the actual issue titles in docs/critic/. Not one line of generic advice.

§7's 'verified state of the repo' inventory is accurate: props really is built with no place() and dependencies ['terrain','roads'], so selectModules() really does exclude it at ?showcase=services — the ownership decision for park vegetation is settled mechanically, not by assertion.

The tooling audit is right: screenshot.mjs has no --eval, camera presets really are inert data (camera.js:36-52), window.__sim.setCamera is debug.js:30 and registry.apis is registry.js:8. The coverage_12 shot is correctly excluded from the gauntlet and given a working Playwright recipe instead.
Item 10 (night) and item 12 (determinism/validation) are model acceptance items: toggled-feature pixel diffs with meanAbs thresholds in both directions, a named grep, and a named prior critic issue.
verdict:
A genuinely strong spec that falls just short of the bar. All ten properties are present, and several are exemplary: the coverage algorithm is defined exactly once with a named degrade path; the catalogue in §4.2 was cross-checked against ui/hud.js and matches on all 17 costs, labels, categories and unlocks; the tick arithmetic (110 ticks from TICKS_PER_HOUR=100/GRID_TICK=50), the 12 288 calls/hour figure (64² × 3 park kinds) and the 13-key list simulation actually queries are all verified-correct rather than plausible; every cited critic issue number is real; and the tooling audit (no --eval, inert presets, coverage_12 excluded from the gauntlet) is accurate. Roughly 14 of 21 acceptance items are mechanically gradable, which is well above the norm here.

Two defects would each plausibly cost a round. First, §7 — the section that exists so nothing is invented — addresses every dependency through `ctx.modules.<dep>.api.<fn>()`, a path that does not exist (registry.js:36 passes the api objects directly), and contradicts §8 and §2 of the same file; with BUILDER.md's mandated optional chaining that failure is silent. Second, five acceptance items are graded in `closeup_12`/`street_12`/`street_22`/`aerial_12`/`skyline_12`, whose framing is fixed by core presets at targets [20,6,20], [40,0,40] and the origin, while §8 forbids the module from declaring anything but its own six names and gives no staging coordinates — so items 5, 7 and 10 turn on where the builder happened to put the buildings, and items 5 and 10 want incompatible content in the same `street` frame. Add the two arithmetic contradictions in §8 (spawnFreeLots(≤120) vs ≥120 buildings; ≥22 items vs a parenthetical summing to 21), item 5's counts having no probe behind them, and the undefined `load`/kind-key behaviour for the two-category incinerator, and a builder is guessing in at least four places that the critic will grade.

Score 8.0 — fix the §7 API paths, pin the camera framings (or allow preset overrides), reconcile §8's counts, and add `stats().decor`, and this is a 9.
